page: Microsoft Azure L64as_v5 is a storage-optimized virtual machine built on Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization and powered by an x86_64 AMD processor. The instance provides 64 dedicated virtual CPUs paired with 512.0 GB of system memory, maintaining a memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware acceleration is absent, with zero GPUs provisioned on this configuration.

A core architectural feature of the L64as_v5 is its integrated high-capacity local storage subsystem, which delivers 15,360 GB of directly attached NVMe SSD storage. It also supports Azure Premium Storage for external managed disk tiers. Networking configurations do not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses, requiring standard Azure virtual network routing or allocated public IPs for external egress and ingress.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the tight integration of 15.36 TB of fast NVMe storage avoids the recurring input/output transaction and provisioning expenses associated with attaching large volumes of networked block storage. The tradeoff lies in the ephemeral nature of direct NVMe media, which requires robust data replication strategies to mitigate host-level maintenance disruptions.

The combination of high compute density, a generous memory footprint, and massive onboard low-latency storage aligns Microsoft Azure L64as_v5 with data-intensive infrastructure. Common target workloads include distributed NoSQL engines, relational database deployments requiring extensive caching and transaction logging, search indexing clusters, and large-scale data analytics pipelines.
